concepts.def: The nerve pathway of a reflex action: receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone in the CNS, motor neurone and effector, giving a fast automatic response.
A junction between two neurones where a neurotransmitter is released, diffuses across the gap and stimulates the next neurone.
A chemical messenger made by an endocrine gland, carried in the blood to target organs where it brings about a response.
The maintenance of a constant internal environment, such as body temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.
A growth response in which a plant shoot grows towards a source of light, controlled by the plant hormone auxin.
A plant hormone that controls growth responses; it gathers on the shaded side of a shoot and promotes cell elongation there.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordination & Response — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordination & Response brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordination & Response.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The correct order of neurones in a reflex arc is:
options: sensory, relay, motor
motor, relay, sensory
relay, motor, sensory
sensory, motor, relay

mcqs.q: The chemical released at a synapse to pass the impulse on is a:
options: neurotransmitter
hormone
enzyme
antibody

mcqs.q: A plant shoot bends towards light because auxin:
options: gathers on the shaded side and makes those cells elongate
is destroyed on the shaded side
stops all growth on the lit side
pulls the cells toward the light

mcqs.q: Hormonal responses differ from nervous responses because hormones:
options: are carried in the blood and act more slowly
travel along nerve fibres
always act faster than nerves
are made by the brain only

mcqs.q: Is a reflex action controlled by conscious thought?
options: Reflexes are controlled by hormones released into the blood.
You decide to carry out a reflex action using your brain.
No - a reflex is processed through a reflex arc in the spinal cord, giving a fast automatic response without a conscious decision.
The shoot bends because the lit side grows faster.

mcqs.q: Why does a shoot bend toward light?
options: Nervous and hormonal responses act at exactly the same speed.
Auxin gathers on the shaded side and makes the cells there elongate more, bending the shoot toward the light.
The shoot bends because light physically pushes it over.
The shoot bends because the lit side grows faster.

mcqs.q: How do hormonal and nervous responses differ?
options: Hormones travel along nerves to reach their targets.
Nervous and hormonal responses act at exactly the same speed.
The shoot bends because the lit side grows faster.
Nervous responses are fast, short-lived and use electrical impulses; hormonal responses are slower, longer-lasting and travel in the blood.
